falsifier: All four pre-registered falsifiers were graded against the shipped parser and the frozen fixture, and three PASS exactly as pre-registered; the fourth is reported PARTIAL because one half of it failed as written and the failure is diagnosed rather than smoothed. (1) 'CS-1-MU-V-NCCD-ETOD-DBETOD-NP parses to CS-1, never CS' — PASS: literal output `kind=base base=CS-1 overlays=[MU, V, NCCD, ETOD, DBETOD, NP]`; the shortest-match control on the SAME input yields `base=CS`, and CS and CS-1 are both table rows, so the truncated reading is a different resolvable district, not a miss. (2) 'A value whose prefix matches no table district returns unrecognised, not a shorter match' — PASS value for value against the CP1 band: I-SF-2 unrecognised/base null (never SF), I-RR unrecognised, SF-4A resolves, bare SF-4 unrecognised (SF-4 is not a row), R&D-CO-NP -> R&D, SF-4.5 unrecognised even with only SF-4 in the vocabulary, empty value unrecognised with a reason. (3) 'The dry run's recognised count for Travis is within the census's Austin district-miss population, and every unrecognised code is listed' — PARTIAL: the second half PASSES in all three legs (2, 3 and 28 distinct unrecognised values, each printed with its parcel count and no truncation, and the fixture test asserts histogram completeness over all 558 live values); the first half FAILED as written (pre-registered band: Travis parcelsRead 380,917 +/- 2%; measured 828,773, 2.18x) and the measured cause is that the CLI's `parcels read` is a FEATURE count while the census counts ACCOUNTS — at account grain the same store measures 380,918 distinct prop_id against the census's 380,917, and 116,421 vs 116,420 (Hays) and 282,570 vs 282,570 (Williamson). (4) 'Removing the longest-match rule fails a fixture' — PASS: the same shipped parseBaseCode with only matchMode swapped fails 0/23 (longest), 1/23 (shortest: CS-1-MU-... -> CS) and 12/23 (first-token, A-164's naive split, which returns null for SF-1/SF-2/SF-3/SF-4A and CS for CS-1-...). Literal outputs are quoted in CP2's falsifiersGraded and reproducible with `npx tsx _scratch/p259-falsifiers.ts`.
contradicted: Two measured contradictions, one of which needs a ruling before the stamp is applied. (A) THE INTERIM FAMILY — the dispatch's parser rule (and CP1's pre-registered band, which names I-SF-2 explicitly) makes every `I-<X>` value unrecognised, and the dry runs show what that costs: 23,499 parcels in Austin zoning polygons publish an interim value (Hays 361: I-RR 272, I-SF-2 89; Williamson 6,108: I-SF-2 5,129, I-RR 734, I-MF-2 245; Travis 17,030 at feature grain: I-SF-2 8,508, I-SF-4A 6,337, I-RR 2,030 and 9 smaller values). The previous reading SERVED those parcels under the base code — the census records no `I-` value anywhere in its 70 Austin rows, while it records the matching base for the same parcels (Hays RR 270 vs I-RR 272, Hays SF-2 88 vs I-SF-2 89, Williamson SF-2 5,946 vs I-SF-2 5,129, Williamson MF-2 347 vs I-MF-2 245) — and the ordinance says the interim district carries its base's standards (City of Austin C2O-2009-017: I-SF-2 follows 'the same regulations used throughout the city in single-family neighborhoods with standard-sized lots'; the city's own 2016 development-standards table gives I-SF-2 setbacks street front 25 ft / interior side 5 ft / rear 10 ft, which is exactly the shipped austin-tx.json SF-2 row: front_ft 25, rear_ft 10, side_ft 5). So shipping as-is turns parcels that were served into district-misses — the census's own defect class, a false absence — for at least the 6,381 Hays+Williamson parcels the census recorded as `value`, and Austin's district misses would RISE in the re-run the dispatch names as this lane's completion condition. The lane did NOT move its pre-registered band and did NOT touch the setback table (both forbidden); the ruling and the two candidate fixes (a declared leading-qualifier rule in the parser, `interimQualifiers: ['I']`, or interim rows in austin-tx.json) are in CP2's theInterimFinding. (B) THE PARCEL COUNTER'S DENOMINATION — `parcels read`/`parcels matched` on the zoning stamp are feature counts (DISTINCT ON feature_index), not account counts, and in Travis the two differ by 2.18x because 423,540 of the county's 828,773 features carry prop_id '0' (no CAD account, empty situs address, 102 tiles) and ~1,200 real accounts hold hundreds of features each (mobile-home parks and condo complexes: one polygon per unit, one account). Any share computed from a feature count in Travis is a share of something other than parcels, and a later `--apply` for austin-tx would write rows for features with no account. Reported, measured, not fixed here (the read path is pre-existing machinery this lane does not own); CP1's Travis band failed because it was written in the census's denomination and measured in the CLI's.

missionPremise: A-164 (measured live 2026-09-15, anonymously) plus P-258 and P-255: Austin's public org 0L95CJ0VTaxqcmED serves PLANNINGCADASTRE_zoning_large_map_scale/FeatureServer/0 at HTTP 200 with 22,504 zoning polygons in state-plane feet (wkid 102739 / latestWkid 2277); its ZONING_BASE collapses codes (plain SF/MF, no numeric suffix) and cannot be used, while ZONING_ZTYPE carries compound values that append overlays and combining districts (SF-3-HD-NP, MF-4-H-CO, CS-1-MU-V-NCCD-ETOD-DBETOD-NP) so the base must be parsed off a prefix and a naive split on '-' yields CS where the base is CS-1; P-258 added the Austin rows to the setback table (28 rows; austin-tx now has 37 districts) and P-255's census line for Austin is the baseline this lane's dry run is compared against. Per the canon preamble the most-current source wins and dates are read at source, which is why the layer's editingInfo.lastEditDate is fetched and recorded per run rather than assumed.
completionPredicate: Done means: Austin's zoning is acquired from the public PLANNINGCADASTRE layer with the projection read and verified at source and the layer's own last-edit date recorded as the vintage; a base-code parser resolves the longest known base district in Austin's table vocabulary, carries overlay/combining suffixes separately, routes planned development to the PUD message, and returns an explicit unrecognised result (never a truncated prefix) when no known base prefixes the value; fixtures exist for the A-164 compound codes and at least 20 sampled live ZONING_ZTYPE values with the fetch time; a dry run covers Austin's Travis/Williamson/Hays parcels and reports base/planned-development/unrecognised counts and the base distribution against the census line; and the four pre-registered falsifiers are graded with evidence. The status is closed-partial, NOT closed, until the stamp is actually applied and P-255's census re-run shows Austin's district misses falling — and per the measurement in `contradicted`, that re-run will only show them falling if the interim `I-` family is resolved first.

fleetMemoryScratch.text: On this Windows box PowerShell's `*>` / `>` redirection writes UTF-16LE. A log read with readFileSync(path,'utf8') is NUL-interleaved and every regex silently misses (symptom this lane hit: 'could not read parcels read' on a line that is visibly present). Detect the FF FE BOM and decode utf16le, or write logs from Node. Cost ~10 minutes of a phantom parsing bug.

`heavy-scan-lease.mjs` looks a lease up BY TOKEN, not by the id `list` prints. Persist id + holderToken + expiry in your scratch the moment you take it, or `renew`/`release` answer LEASE_LOST (409) and the only remaining exit is natural expiry. This lane lost the Hays-leg token that way.

`zoning-stamp`'s `parcels read` / `parcels matched` are FEATURE counts (DISTINCT ON feature_index), while the census's per-county `parcels` is an ACCOUNT count (distinct prop_id). Convert before comparing; in Travis the ratio is 2.18x. Write dry-run bands in the same denomination the instrument reports, and say which denomination that is.

Trying to reach the previous Austin zoning source `Publish_Zoning_AGOL` for a vintage comparison: the service is now token-gated (HTTP 200 with ArcGIS error 499 'Token Required' even for ?f=json). Use P-255's census as the record of the previous reading instead.

Treating a 4th-quarter `count(*)` on txgio_parcel per county as cheap: a Travis count took 61s (and 240s before that under contention). pg_class.reltuples and pg_stats MCVs answer the sizing questions in milliseconds; use count(DISTINCT ...) only when the distinct value itself is the deliverable.
